svg.title: Required inspections: annual, 100-hour and the other checks
svg.desc: Annual inspection within the preceding 12 calendar months for aircraft not flown for hire, done by an A&P mechanic with inspection authorization, a repair station or the manufacturer. 100-hour inspection for aircraft carrying passengers for hire or used for paid flight instruction; the 100-hour limit may be exceeded by no more than 10 hours to reach a place where the inspection can be done, and the excess counts toward the next 100 hours. Altimeter system and transponder checks every 24 months, ELT every 12 calendar months with battery replacement rules.
svg.text: Required inspections: annual, 100-hour and the other checks
The owner or operator has the primary responsibility for keeping the aircraft airworthy. All aircraft
need inspecting at least once every 12 calendar months; some need it after every 100 hours.
Annual inspection
Applies to small aircraft (12,500 pounds or less)
with a reciprocating engine or a single-engine
turbojet/turbopropeller, flown for business or
pleasure and not for compensation or hire
Done by an A&P mechanic holding an inspection
authorization (IA), by the manufacturer, or by an
appropriately rated repair station
Must have been performed within the preceding 12
calendar months: from any day of a month to the
last day of the same month the following year
Overdue: a Special Flight Permit may allow a
flight to where the inspection can be done, but
all applicable ADs that are due must be complied
with before the flight
100-hour inspection
Required within the preceding 100 hours of time
in service, and the aircraft approved for return
to service
Applies to aircraft under 12,500 pounds (except
multi-engine turbojet/turboprop airplanes and
turbine rotorcraft) used to carry passengers for
hire
Also applies to an aircraft used for flight
instruction for hire, when provided by the person
giving the instruction
Done by an A&P mechanic, an appropriately rated
repair station, or the manufacturer
An annual inspection, or an inspection for
issuing an Airworthiness Certificate, may be
substituted
The 10-hour allowance on the 100-hour limit
100 hours of time in service
inspection done
+ no more than 10 hours
May be exceeded by no more than 10
hours, only to travel to a
location where the inspection can
be performed.
Any excess time used for this purpose must be included in computing the next 100 hours of time in service.
Other required checks
Altimeter system (altimeter, encoding altimeter
and related system): tested and inspected within
the 24 months before operating in controlled
airspace under IFR
Transponder: tested and inspected within the 24
months before use, regardless of airspace
restrictions
ELT: inspected within 12 calendar months after
the last inspection (installation, battery
corrosion, controls and crash sensor, sufficient
signal from the antenna)
ELT battery: replaced or recharged after more
than 1 cumulative hour of use, or when 50 percent
of its useful life has expired
Preflight and other programs
Preflight inspection: the systematic means by
which the pilot decides whether the aircraft is
airworthy and in condition for safe operation;
the POH has a section for it
The annual and 100-hour requirements do not apply
to large (over 12,500 pounds) airplanes,
turbojets, multi-engine turbopropeller airplanes,
or aircraft on a progressive inspection program
Some aircraft are inspected under a system based
on calendar time, time in service, number of
system operations, or a combination
All inspections should follow the current
manufacturer maintenance manual, including the
Instructions for Continued Airworthiness
